notes: Relative time expressions are interpreted relative to the available order history, not the current date.
Expected SQL and expected results will be added only after verification against the PostgreSQL database.
Evaluation should compare executed results rather than exact SQL strings.

benchmark.question: How many customers do we have in total?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customer;

benchmark.question: How many products are currently marked as discontinued?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_product_count FROM product WHERE discontinued = '1';

benchmark.question: How many employees work for the company?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employee;

benchmark.question: How many distinct shipping companies do we use?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS shipper_count FROM shipper;

benchmark.question: How many suppliers are based in the USA?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS usa_supplier_count FROM supplier WHERE country = 'USA';

benchmark.question: What is the average unit price across all products?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT AVG(unitprice) AS average_unit_price FROM product;

benchmark.question: How many product categories do we sell?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS category_count FROM category;

benchmark.question: How many territories are assigned to each region?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT r.regiondescription AS region, COUNT(t.territoryid) AS territory_count FROM region r LEFT JOIN territory t ON t.regionid=r.regionid GROUP BY r.regionid,r.regiondescription ORDER BY r.regionid;

benchmark.question: What was our total revenue in 2007?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS total_revenue FROM salesorder so JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid WHERE so.orderdate>=DATE '2007-01-01' AND so.orderdate<DATE '2008-01-01';

benchmark.question: How many orders has each employee handled?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname,COUNT(so.orderid) AS order_count FROM employee e LEFT JOIN salesorder so ON so.empid=e.empid GROUP BY e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname ORDER BY e.empid;

benchmark.question: What is the total quantity sold for each product category?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT c.categoryid,c.categoryname,COALESCE(SUM(od.qty),0) AS total_quantity_sold FROM category c LEFT JOIN product p ON p.categoryid=c.categoryid LEFT JOIN orderdetail od ON od.productid=p.productid GROUP BY c.categoryid,c.categoryname ORDER BY c.categoryid;

benchmark.question: How many orders has each customer placed?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT c.custid,c.companyname,COUNT(so.orderid) AS order_count FROM customer c LEFT JOIN salesorder so ON so.custid=c.custid GROUP BY c.custid,c.companyname ORDER BY c.custid;

benchmark.question: What is the average order value per customer?
benchmark.expected_sql: WITH order_totals AS (SELECT so.orderid,so.custid,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS order_value FROM salesorder so JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid GROUP BY so.orderid,so.custid) SELECT c.custid,c.companyname,AVG(ot.order_value) AS average_order_value FROM customer c LEFT JOIN order_totals ot ON ot.custid=c.custid GROUP BY c.custid,c.companyname ORDER BY c.custid;

benchmark.question: How many distinct products does each supplier provide?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT s.supplierid,s.companyname,COUNT(DISTINCT p.productid) AS product_count FROM supplier s LEFT JOIN product p ON p.supplierid=s.supplierid GROUP BY s.supplierid,s.companyname ORDER BY s.supplierid;

benchmark.question: What is the total freight cost associated with each shipper?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT sh.shipperid,sh.companyname,COALESCE(SUM(so.freight),0) AS total_freight FROM shipper sh LEFT JOIN salesorder so ON so.shipperid=sh.shipperid GROUP BY sh.shipperid,sh.companyname ORDER BY sh.shipperid;

benchmark.question: How many orders were shipped by each shipping company?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT sh.shipperid,sh.companyname,COUNT(so.orderid) AS order_count FROM shipper sh LEFT JOIN salesorder so ON so.shipperid=sh.shipperid GROUP BY sh.shipperid,sh.companyname ORDER BY sh.shipperid;

benchmark.question: Which orders were placed in the year 2008?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM salesorder WHERE orderdate>=DATE '2008-01-01' AND orderdate<DATE '2009-01-01' ORDER BY orderdate,orderid;

benchmark.question: Which customers are located in London?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT custid,companyname,contactname,city,country FROM customer WHERE city='London' ORDER BY custid;

benchmark.question: Which products currently have fewer than 10 units in stock?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT productid,productname,unitsinstock FROM product WHERE unitsinstock<10 ORDER BY productid;

benchmark.question: Which orders had a freight cost greater than 100?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT orderid,custid,orderdate,freight FROM salesorder WHERE freight>100 ORDER BY freight DESC,orderid;

benchmark.question: Which orders were shipped after their required delivery date?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT orderid,custid,orderdate,requireddate,shippeddate FROM salesorder WHERE shippeddate>requireddate ORDER BY orderdate,orderid;

benchmark.question: Which employees were hired before 1994?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT empid,firstname,lastname,hiredate FROM employee WHERE hiredate<DATE '1994-01-01' ORDER BY hiredate,empid;

benchmark.question: Which products belong to the 'Beverages' category?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT p.productid,p.productname FROM product p JOIN category c ON c.categoryid=p.categoryid WHERE c.categoryname='Beverages' ORDER BY p.productid;

benchmark.question: Which employee processed the most orders for customers based in France?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname,COUNT(so.orderid) AS order_count FROM employee e JOIN salesorder so ON so.empid=e.empid JOIN customer c ON c.custid=so.custid WHERE c.country='France' GROUP BY e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname ORDER BY order_count DESC,e.empid LIMIT 1;

benchmark.question: List the products supplied by suppliers based in Japan.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT p.productid,p.productname,s.companyname AS supplier FROM product p JOIN supplier s ON s.supplierid=p.supplierid WHERE s.country='Japan' ORDER BY p.productid;

benchmark.question: Show the names of customers who have ordered products from the 'Seafood' category.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.custid,c.companyname,c.contactname FROM customer c JOIN salesorder so ON so.custid=c.custid JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid JOIN product p ON p.productid=od.productid JOIN category cat ON cat.categoryid=p.categoryid WHERE cat.categoryname='Seafood' ORDER BY c.custid;

benchmark.question: Which shipping companies have delivered orders for customers in Germany?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT sh.shipperid,sh.companyname FROM shipper sh JOIN salesorder so ON so.shipperid=sh.shipperid JOIN customer c ON c.custid=so.custid WHERE c.country='Germany' ORDER BY sh.shipperid;

benchmark.question: List all orders along with the name of the employee who handled each one.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT so.orderid,so.custid,so.orderdate,e.firstname,e.lastname FROM salesorder so JOIN employee e ON e.empid=so.empid ORDER BY so.orderid;

benchmark.question: Which suppliers provide products in the 'Condiments' category?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT s.supplierid,s.companyname FROM supplier s JOIN product p ON p.supplierid=s.supplierid JOIN category c ON c.categoryid=p.categoryid WHERE c.categoryname='Condiments' ORDER BY s.supplierid;

benchmark.question: Show the order details for all orders placed by customers in Spain.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT so.orderid,od.productid,od.unitprice,od.qty,od.discount FROM salesorder so JOIN customer c ON c.custid=so.custid JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid WHERE c.country='Spain' ORDER BY so.orderid,od.productid;

benchmark.question: List each employee along with the name of their manager.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname,m.firstname AS manager_firstname,m.lastname AS manager_lastname FROM employee e LEFT JOIN employee m ON m.empid=e.mgrid ORDER BY e.empid;

benchmark.question: What is the month-over-month revenue trend for 2007, accounting for discounts?
benchmark.expected_sql: WITH monthly_revenue AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month',so.orderdate)::date AS month,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS revenue FROM salesorder so JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid WHERE so.orderdate>=DATE '2007-01-01' AND so.orderdate<DATE '2008-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month',so.orderdate)) SELECT month,revenue,LAG(revenue) OVER(ORDER BY month) AS previous_month_revenue,revenue-LAG(revenue) OVER(ORDER BY month) AS month_over_month_change FROM monthly_revenue ORDER BY month;

benchmark.question: Which customers placed at least one order in every quarter of 2008?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT c.custid,c.companyname FROM customer c JOIN salesorder so ON so.custid=c.custid WHERE so.orderdate>=DATE '2008-01-01' AND so.orderdate<DATE '2009-01-01' GROUP BY c.custid,c.companyname HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM so.orderdate))=4 ORDER BY c.custid;

benchmark.question: What is the average discount applied per product category?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT c.categoryid,c.categoryname,AVG(od.discount) AS average_discount FROM category c JOIN product p ON p.categoryid=c.categoryid JOIN orderdetail od ON od.productid=p.productid GROUP BY c.categoryid,c.categoryname ORDER BY c.categoryid;

benchmark.question: Which products have generated more than $10,000 in total revenue, after accounting for discounts?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT p.productid,p.productname,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS total_revenue FROM product p JOIN orderdetail od ON od.productid=p.productid GROUP BY p.productid,p.productname HAVING SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount))>10000 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC,p.productid;

benchmark.question: Rank employees by the total revenue generated from the orders they handled.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS total_revenue FROM employee e JOIN salesorder so ON so.empid=e.empid JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid GROUP BY e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname ORDER BY total_revenue DESC,e.empid;

benchmark.question: What percentage of total line-item revenue came from order details with a discount greater than 0?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT 100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN od.discount>0 THEN od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount) ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)),0) AS discounted_revenue_percentage FROM orderdetail od;

benchmark.question: Which customers' total spending exceeds the average total spending across all customers?
benchmark.expected_sql: WITH customer_spending AS (SELECT c.custid,c.companyname,COALESCE(SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)),0) AS total_spending FROM customer c LEFT JOIN salesorder so ON so.custid=c.custid LEFT JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid GROUP BY c.custid,c.companyname) SELECT custid,companyname,total_spending FROM customer_spending WHERE total_spending>(SELECT AVG(total_spending) FROM customer_spending) ORDER BY total_spending DESC,custid;

benchmark.question: Show me our top customers.
benchmark.ambiguity_reason: The metric defining 'top' is not specified.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: When you say 'top' customers, do you mean by total revenue, by number of orders placed, or by average order value?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT c.custid,c.companyname,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS total_revenue FROM customer c JOIN salesorder so ON so.custid=c.custid JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid GROUP BY c.custid,c.companyname ORDER BY total_revenue DESC,c.custid LIMIT 10;

benchmark.question: Which products performed best in 2007?
benchmark.ambiguity_reason: The metric defining 'performed best' is not specified.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: Should 'best performing' be measured by total revenue, by quantity sold, or by number of orders?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT p.productid,p.productname,SUM(od.qty) AS total_quantity_sold FROM product p JOIN orderdetail od ON od.productid=p.productid JOIN salesorder so ON so.orderid=od.orderid WHERE so.orderdate>=DATE '2007-01-01' AND so.orderdate<DATE '2008-01-01' GROUP BY p.productid,p.productname ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC,p.productid LIMIT 10;

benchmark.question: Who are our most valuable suppliers?
benchmark.ambiguity_reason: The metric defining 'valuable' is not specified.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: Would you like suppliers ranked by the total revenue generated from their products, or by the number of products they supply?
benchmark.clarification_answer: By total revenue generated from their products.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT s.supplierid,s.companyname,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS total_revenue FROM supplier s JOIN product p ON p.supplierid=s.supplierid JOIN orderdetail od ON od.productid=p.productid GROUP BY s.supplierid,s.companyname ORDER BY total_revenue DESC,s.supplierid LIMIT 10;

benchmark.question: Give me a list of our best employees.
benchmark.ambiguity_reason: The metric defining 'best' is not specified.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: Should employees be ranked by total revenue from their orders, or by the number of orders they've handled?
benchmark.clarification_answer: By the number of orders they've handled.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname,COUNT(so.orderid) AS order_count FROM employee e LEFT JOIN salesorder so ON so.empid=e.empid GROUP BY e.empid,e.firstname,e.lastname ORDER BY order_count DESC,e.empid LIMIT 10;

benchmark.question: Show me the most successful product categories.
benchmark.ambiguity_reason: The metric defining 'successful' is not specified.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: Do you want categories ranked by total revenue or by total quantity sold?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT c.categoryid,c.categoryname,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS total_revenue FROM category c JOIN product p ON p.categoryid=c.categoryid JOIN orderdetail od ON od.productid=p.productid GROUP BY c.categoryid,c.categoryname ORDER BY total_revenue DESC,c.categoryid LIMIT 10;

benchmark.question: Which customers should we prioritize for outreach?
benchmark.ambiguity_reason: The business criteria for outreach priority are not specified.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: What should define priority here—recent inactivity, historical spending, or another criterion?
benchmark.clarification_answer: Customers who placed no orders during the final 6 months of the available order history but whose earlier total spending exceeded $5,000.
benchmark.expected_sql: WITH customer_spending AS (SELECT c.custid,c.companyname,SUM(CASE WHEN so.orderdate<DATE '2007-11-06' THEN od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount) ELSE 0 END) AS earlier_spending,COUNT(DISTINCT so.orderid) FILTER (WHERE so.orderdate>=DATE '2007-11-06' AND so.orderdate<=DATE '2008-05-06') AS recent_orders FROM customer c LEFT JOIN salesorder so ON so.custid=c.custid LEFT JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid GROUP BY c.custid,c.companyname) SELECT custid,companyname,earlier_spending FROM customer_spending WHERE recent_orders=0 AND earlier_spending>5000 ORDER BY earlier_spending DESC,custid;

benchmark.question: What are our strongest markets?
benchmark.ambiguity_reason: Both the meaning of 'market' and the metric for 'strongest' are unspecified.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: By 'markets', do you mean countries, regions, or cities—and should 'strongest' be measured by total revenue or number of customers?
benchmark.clarification_answer: By country, measured by total revenue.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT c.country,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS total_revenue FROM customer c JOIN salesorder so ON so.custid=c.custid JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY total_revenue DESC,c.country;

benchmark.question: What are our recent orders?
benchmark.suggested_clarification: What time period should I use to define 'recent' orders?
benchmark.clarification_answer: Orders placed during the final 30 days of the available order history.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT orderid,custid,orderdate FROM salesorder WHERE orderdate>=TIMESTAMP '2008-04-06 00:00:00' AND orderdate<=TIMESTAMP '2008-05-06 00:00:00' ORDER BY orderdate,orderid;

benchmark.question: Which products are considered expensive?
benchmark.suggested_clarification: What unit-price threshold should define an expensive product?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT productid,productname,unitprice FROM product WHERE unitprice>=50 ORDER BY unitprice DESC,productid;

benchmark.question: Show me our active customers.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: Should 'active' mean customers who ordered within a specific recent time frame, and if so, what time frame?
benchmark.clarification_answer: Customers who placed at least one order during the final 90 days of the available order history.
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT c.custid,c.companyname FROM customer c JOIN salesorder so ON so.custid=c.custid WHERE so.orderdate>=TIMESTAMP '2008-02-06 00:00:00' AND so.orderdate<=TIMESTAMP '2008-05-06 00:00:00' GROUP BY c.custid,c.companyname ORDER BY c.custid;

benchmark.question: Which orders would you consider large orders?
benchmark.ambiguity_reason: 'Large' could refer to quantity or total dollar value.
benchmark.suggested_clarification: Should 'large' orders be defined by total quantity of items, or by total dollar value?
benchmark.expected_sql: SELECT so.orderid,SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount)) AS order_value FROM salesorder so JOIN orderdetail od ON od.orderid=so.orderid GROUP BY so.orderid HAVING SUM(od.unitprice*od.qty*(1-od.discount))>1000 ORDER BY order_value DESC,so.orderid;
